# NPDev DSL keyword reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/docs/generate_dsl_keyword_reference.py from NPDevContract/schemas/model.schema.json, NPDevContract/schemas/pack.schema.json and scripts/policy/dsl-keyword-meanings/*.json. Do not edit by hand: edit the schema or the meanings data, then run the script. -->

The complete list of keywords an NPDev model (`model.json`) or pack (`pack.json`) may use: what each one means, where it may appear, whether it is required, and which values it accepts. Every keyword of the DSL is here; a key that is not here is rejected by the schema (`additionalProperties: false`).

Schema version `1.0.0`, DSL version `3.0.0`. **759 keywords** are documented: 719 declared by the model schema (100 object kinds) and 40 by the pack schema, counted exactly as `scripts/quality/check-dsl-keyword-budget.py` counts them. The model root keys are listed separately in section 0.

## How to read this reference

- A model is a tree of **object kinds**. Each kind below is one `$defs` entry of the schema and has its own table of keywords. The heading is the kind's schema name; **Used in** says which parent keyword holds it (`concept.fields` means the `fields` array of a `concept`; `root:flows` / `flows` means the top-level `flows` array of a model file; `pack:` means a pack file).
- **Required** is the JSON Schema `required` list of that kind. Some kinds add an either/or rule the schema expresses with `oneOf`/`allOf`; those are stated in the kind's summary.
- **Type** names the JSON shape. A name in brackets is another object kind (a link to its section). "one of" lists the closed set of allowed values. Any array of object kinds at the model root also accepts `{"$ref": "path/to/file.json"}` entries that pull the item from a local file.
- Entries marked *Legacy* or *Retiring* still validate but are on their way out; do not use them in new models.
- Expressions (`where`, `visibleWhen`, `defaultExpression`, ...) use the one NPDev expression language (`docs/EXPRESSIONS.md`). Flows are described in `docs/FLOWS.md`, screens in `docs/SCREEN_TAXONOMY.md` and `docs/UI_CONTRACT.md`, packs in `docs/PACK_DESIGN.md`.

## 0. Model root and pack file

A model file is one JSON object. `namespace` and `concepts` are required in every model (the schema also requires `version`); everything else is optional. Each array below holds objects of the kind named in its type, and every array of object kinds also accepts an entry of the form `{"$ref": "relative/file.json"}` that pulls that item from a local file next to the model. The keys are grouped by the twelve nouns of the vocabulary in the sections that follow.

### Model root keys

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `string` | optional | Optional URL of the JSON Schema, for editor completion. |
| `schemaVersion` | fixed `"1.0.0"` | optional | Version of the model file container; always `1.0.0`. |
| `dslVersion` | fixed `"3.0.0"` | optional | Optional. Model-format version; defaults to 3.0.0 (the unified-vocabulary DSL). |
| `namespace` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The model's namespace (required): the Java package root of the generated app and the prefix of generated identifiers. |
| `version` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The model's own version string (required), for example `1.0.0`. |
| `concepts` | array of [`concept`](#concept) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) (min items 1) | required | The record types of the app (required, at least one). See Concept. |
| `domainTypes` | array of [`domainType`](#domaintype) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Reusable named field types. |
| `capabilities` | array of [`capability`](#capability) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Outbound operations and inbound webhooks to the outside world. |
| `events` | array of [`event`](#event) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Named facts that flows publish, trigger on and await. |
| `flows` | array of [`flow`](#flow) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | What the app does: durable step lists started by a trigger. |
| `queries` | array of [`query`](#query) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Named, parameterised reads over concepts. |
| `conversions` | array of [`conversion`](#conversion) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Declarative data conversions applied at boot when the schema changes. |
| `panels` | array of [`panel`](#panel) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Hand-composed screens (the older way; screens are the current one). |
| `autoPanels` | array of [`autoPanel`](#autopanel) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (a `$ref` to a local JSON file) | optional | Panels generated from a concept or aggregate (the older way; screens are the current one). |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes about the model. Never carries behavior. |
| `packs` | array of [`packRef`](#packref) | optional | The packs this model consumes, each a local file or a remote coordinate. |
| `provides` | object | optional | What this app satisfies for a pack's own `requires` (roles/capabilities/network) -- a pack's requirement unbound here refuses composition, naming the pack, its path, and the unbound key.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`roles` (array of `string`; optional): Roles this app provides for packs' `requires.roles`.<br>`capabilities` (array of `string`; optional): Capabilities this app provides for packs' `requires.capabilities`.<br>`network` (array of `string`; optional): Hosts this app allows packs to reach.<br>`roleBindings` (map of name to `string`; optional): Maps each logical role name used by a pack (`role('name')`) to this app's concrete role. |
| `externalAi` | [`externalAi`](#externalai) | optional | The opt-in to delegating work to an outside AI, with vendors, prompts and limits. |
| `roles` | array of [`role`](#role) | optional | The kinds of user and what each may do. |
| `propertyScopes` | array of [`propertyScope`](#propertyscope) | optional | The scoped-property cascade's declared levels, ORDER = resolution order, most specific first. The least-specific level is not declared here -- it is each property's own 'default'. |
| `properties` | array of [`property`](#property) | optional | Declared runtime properties resolved through the scoped-property cascade (see propertyScopes). |
| `modules` | array of [`context`](#context) | optional | bounded-context declarations. Each names a context and $ref's the fragment file (composed via the same pack/fragment $ref machinery as `fragments`/`packs`) whose concepts/queries/panels/flows belong to that context. Cross-context references use context::Concept (D1); a fragment may only reference a context its own `imports[]` (pack.schema.json) declares (D3) -- an undeclared or unresolvable reference is a compile error, never silent. |
| `sequences` | array of [`sequence`](#sequence) | optional | model-declared document-numbering counters (e.g. INV-2026-0001). A field's defaultExpression can call nextNumber('name') to atomically allocate the next value, formatted per this sequence's format template. |
| `fieldConventions` | array of [`fieldConvention`](#fieldconvention) | optional | Field naming conventions: {match, defaults} rules typing a concept field that declares no `type` (e.g. {"match": "*Dt", "defaults": {"type": "date"}}). Built-in rules (conventions-basic) are always active at the lowest priority. A pack may declare them too. |
| `functions` | array of [`function`](#function) | optional | Named pure functions callable from any expression, e.g. surgeMultiplier(open, free). Each call is replaced by the function body at compile time, so functions cost no runtime. A pack's functions are called as pack::name. |
| `experiences` | array of [`experience`](#experience) | optional | Experiences per role -- who lands where, on which device. Order matters: a signed-in user lands in the first experience whose `for` contains one of their roles. See screens[]. |
| `screens` | array of [`screen`](#screen) | optional | The screens experiences navigate to, each one archetype from a closed set (list, detail, form, status, inbox, board, map, dashboard, workbench, document, picker, custom). Screen names are unique across the model. |
| `seeds` | array of [`seed`](#seed) | optional | model/pack-declared seed rows, reusing the existing app-level seed record shape (NPDevContract/schemas/seed.schema.json's $defs/record). Applied once, automatically, at first boot through the same governed ConceptGateway.save path every other write uses (see com.finalexec.seed.ModelSeedRunner in NPDevRuntimeHost); regenerating/restarting the app does not duplicate rows. A pack/context-declared seed's concept must name a concept the SAME pack/context owns -- rewritten to its pack-qualified form at composition time, and a seed naming a concept the pack does not own is a compile error (see ModelSourceResolver's seeds handling and SeedValidation). |
| `backOffice` | [`backOffice`](#backoffice) | optional | Optional configuration of the generated back office. |
| `agentAccess` | [`agentAccess`](#agentaccess) | optional | What AI agents are offered and on which channels. |

### Pack file keys

A pack file (`pack.json`) is a named, versioned bundle of the same kinds of members a model declares (concepts, flows, capabilities, roles, screens, ...) that other models consume through the `packs` root key. The member arrays have the same shape as in a model; the keys that only exist in a pack file describe the pack itself (identity, dependencies, publishing metadata).

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `string` | optional | Optional URL of the JSON Schema, for editor completion. |
| `dslVersion` | fixed `"3.0.0"` | required | The DSL version the pack is written in (required); `3.0.0`. |
| `pack` | `string` (min length 1; pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`) | required | Pack identifier (lowercase, no spaces). Used as the namespace prefix for all definitions contributed by this pack. |
| `namespace` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional Java/package namespace for generated code. |
| `version` | `string` (min length 1; pattern `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`) | required | The pack's own version (required), `major.minor.patch`. |
| `description` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A sentence saying what the pack provides. |
| `packs` | array of object | optional | Transitive pack dependencies. `version` is a minimal constraint: an exact version (`2.0.3`) or a caret constraint (`^2.0`, same major, minor and patch at least as high). An entry may also declare `from` (a remote coordinate, same grammar as the model's `packRef.from`) or `$ref` (a local file); with neither, the local file `packs/<packId>/pack.json` is used.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`pack` (`string`; optional; min length 1; pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`): Identifier of the dependency pack.<br>`version` (`string`; optional; min length 1; pattern `^(\^)?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$`): Minimal version constraint: exact (`2.0.3`) or caret (`^2.0`, same major).<br>`from` (`string`; optional; min length 1; must match the schema's pattern): Remote pack coordinate for a transitive dependency -- same grammar as model.schema.json's packRef `from`. Mutually exclusive with `$ref`.<br>`$ref` (`string`; optional; min length 1; pattern `^(?![A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:)(?!/).*\.json$`): Explicit local file for a transitive dependency, overriding the default `packs/<packId>/pack.json` convention. Mutually exclusive with `from`. |
| `requires` | object | optional | What this pack needs from the composing app (or from a transitive importer's own provides). Composition refuses when a requirement is unbound -- see model.schema.json's root `provides`.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`roles` (array of `string`; optional): Roles the composing app must provide.<br>`capabilities` (array of `string`; optional): Capabilities the composing app must provide.<br>`network` (array of `string`; optional): Hosts the pack needs network access to. |
| `concepts` | array of [`concept`](#concept) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) (min items 1) | optional | Concepts the pack contributes; consumers reference them as `pack::Concept`. |
| `domainTypes` | array of [`domainType`](#domaintype) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Domain types the pack contributes. |
| `capabilities` | array of [`capability`](#capability) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Capabilities the pack contributes. |
| `events` | array of [`event`](#event) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Events the pack contributes. |
| `flows` | array of [`flow`](#flow) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Flows the pack contributes. |
| `queries` | array of [`query`](#query) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Queries the pack contributes. |
| `conversions` | array of [`conversion`](#conversion) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Data conversions the pack contributes. |
| `panels` | array of [`panel`](#panel) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Panels the pack contributes. |
| `autoPanels` | array of [`autoPanel`](#autopanel) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Auto panels the pack contributes. |
| `backOffice` | object | optional | The back-office guide pages this pack contributes (it was the pack-level guidePages). Composition qualifies each page like any other member (packId::PageName) and appends it, after the model's own pages, to the composed model's root backOffice.pages.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`pages` (array of [`guidePage`](#guidepage) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref); optional): Guide pages the pack adds to the composed model's back office. |
| `roles` | array of [`role`](#role) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Roles the pack contributes. |
| `sequences` | array of [`sequence`](#sequence) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | A pack may declare document-numbering counters alongside its other members. `name` is never namespace-qualified by pack composition (see model.schema.json's sequence $def). |
| `fieldConventions` | array of [`fieldConvention`](#fieldconvention) | optional | Field naming conventions this pack contributes: {match, defaults} rules typing a concept field that declares no `type`, in the importing model and in every pack. Lower priority than the model's own rules. |
| `functions` | array of [`function`](#function) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Named pure functions a pack provides (rung 2 of the extension ladder). Consumers call them as &lt;pack&gt;::&lt;name&gt;; inside the pack the bare name works. |
| `experiences` | array of [`experience`](#experience) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | A pack may declare experiences/screens alongside its other members. Their `name` is never namespace-qualified by pack composition (see model.schema.json's experiences property); references out of them (roles, concept, query, flow) are. |
| `screens` | array of [`screen`](#screen) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | A pack may declare experiences/screens alongside its other members. Their `name` is never namespace-qualified by pack composition (see model.schema.json's experiences property); references out of them (roles, concept, query, flow) are. |
| `seeds` | array of [`seed`](#seed) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | A pack may declare first-boot seed rows alongside its other members. `concept` MUST name a concept this SAME pack declares -- rewritten to its pack-qualified form by pack composition, and a seed naming a concept the pack does not own is a compile error (see model.schema.json's seed $def and ModelSourceResolver's seeds handling). |
| `propertyScopes` | array of [`propertyScope`](#propertyscope) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Property scopes the pack contributes. |
| `properties` | array of [`property`](#property) or [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Properties the pack contributes. |
| `imports` | array of `string` | optional | The other bounded contexts this context fragment may reference via context::Concept (D1). An unlisted context named in a context::Concept reference is a compile error, never a silent resolve-to-nothing (D3, X0). The import graph must be acyclic -- a cycle is a compile error, not a warning. |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes about the pack. |
| `augments` | object | optional | Declares this pack AUGMENTS (adds to) a concept owned by another pack -- not a new kind of thing (that is `specializes`). The extension pack contributes fields to the target concept via PackExtensionComposer (additive-only, sealedness/collision refusal). The old `extends` key and the `metadata.extends` convention are gone.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`pack` (`string`; required; min length 1): The pack id of the base pack whose concept is being augmented.<br>`concept` (`string`; required; min length 1): The bare concept name in the base pack that this pack adds fields to. |
| `fragments` | array of [`localModelRef`](#localmodelref) | optional | Local files whose members are merged into the pack. |
| `category` | one of `security`, `web-ui`, `crypto`, `bots`, `ai-tools`, `finance`, `math`, `other` | optional | Author-ecosystem catalog grouping shown in the Store panel's drill-down. |
| `author` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Free-text attribution for who published this pack. |
| `forkedFrom` | object | optional | Attribution when this pack was derived from another published pack.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`pack` (`string`; required; min length 1): Identifier of the pack this one was derived from.<br>`version` (`string`; required; min length 1): Version of the original pack at the time of the fork.<br>`originAuthor` (`string`; optional): Author of the original pack. |
| `migrations` | map of name to array of object (one of 4 alternative shapes) | optional | The migration-replay chain for this pack's version history, keyed '&lt;oldVersion&gt; -&gt; &lt;newVersion&gt;' (e.g. "1.0.0 -&gt; 1.1.0"). `npdev pack publish` auto-populates an empty array here for every non-BREAKING (ADDITIVE/PATCH-only, or no-op) version bump -- see com.npdev.dsl.v1.pack.PackPublishGate. A non-empty array is hand-authored by the pack author for a BREAKING bump, one op per DSL-level change the hop actually made; com.npdev.dsl.v1.pack.PackMigrationComposer composes hops across a multi-version jump and synthesizes the renamedFrom markers com.npdev.dsl.v1.pack.PackMigrationChainSynthesizer injects before the app model is generated. Once published, a hop's array is immutable -- see PackPublishGate's chain-immutability check.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`op` (fixed `"renameField"`; required): The migration step kind: `renameField`, `renameConcept`, `addField` or `dropField`.<br>`concept` (`string`; required; min length 1): The concept the step applies to.<br>`from` (`string`; required; min length 1): Old name.<br>`to` (`string`; required; min length 1): New name.<br>`op` (fixed `"renameConcept"`; required): The migration step kind: `renameField`, `renameConcept`, `addField` or `dropField`.<br>`op` (fixed `"addField"`; required): The migration step kind: `renameField`, `renameConcept`, `addField` or `dropField`.<br>`field` (`string`; required; min length 1): The field the step adds or drops.<br>`op` (fixed `"dropField"`; required): The migration step kind: `renameField`, `renameConcept`, `addField` or `dropField`. |
| `firstPublishedVersion` | `string` (pattern `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`) | optional | The pack's own true first-ever-published version, pinned once by `npdev pack publish --write` (either at this pack's first publish under this field's existence, backfilled from its migrations chain's own earliest hop, or -- for a pack with no chain yet -- copied from its own current `version`) and immutable thereafter, exactly like a migrations hop (see PackPublishGate's chain-immutability check). Exists as a trust anchor independent of the migrations chain's own current content: PackDependencyGraphWalker's untracked-pack fallback prefers this field over PackMigrationChain.earliestFromVersion() (which can be fooled if the chain's own earliest hop is later removed/truncated by a hand-edit that bypasses the publish gate). |
| `private` | array of `string` | optional | Bare member names (from concepts/capabilities/procedures/events/... -- any of the kinds this pack declares) that exist for this pack's own internal use only. A reference to '&lt;thisPack&gt;::&lt;name&gt;' from outside this pack -- another pack, a context, or the composing app's own root model -- refuses composition, naming the pack and the member. This pack's own members may still reference each other freely regardless of privacy (visibility only gates access from OUTSIDE the declaring pack). Absent (the default, and every pack's behavior before this field existed): every member is public. |
| `extensionPoints` | array of `string` | optional | Bare names -- normally a subset of `private` -- that a consuming app or pack MAY specialize (via `specializes`/`extends`) despite being private. Unlike full public membership, an extension point may still not be referenced directly (as a domain type, a query concept, a flow's scope, etc.) -- only named as the base of a specialization. |
| `signature` | object | optional | Cryptographic signature of the pack's content digest. The digest is the same SHA-256 tree hash PackCache computes for content-addressed storage; the signature is that digest signed with a keypair (Ed25519 or SHA256withRSA). The public key is embedded so a consumer can verify without out-of-band key distribution. When present, `npdev pack add` verifies the signature against the cached digest and refuses on mismatch.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`algorithm` (one of `Ed25519`, `SHA256withRSA`; required): The signing algorithm: `Ed25519` or `SHA256withRSA`.<br>`digest` (`string`; required; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`): The signed SHA-256 content digest, `sha256:<hex>`.<br>`value` (`string`; required): Base64-encoded signature of the digest<br>`publicKey` (`string`; required): Base64-encoded public key for verification |
| `deprecated` | object | optional | Marks a published pack VERSION as deprecated. Authored into pack.json BEFORE that version is published, so this block becomes ordinary, immutable content of the version it describes -- never a retroactive edit to an already-published file. `npdev pack deprecate` writes it; `npdev pack add`/`update` warn when a resolved pack's locked version carries it, naming `supersededBy` when present; `--strict` refuses instead of warning when `supersededBy` is present (with no successor named there is nothing to redirect the refusal to, so it only warns).<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`since` (`string`; required; pattern `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`): The exact pack version this deprecation takes effect from -- normally equal to this pack.json's own `version`.<br>`reason` (`string`; required; min length 1): Why the version is deprecated.<br>`supersededBy` (object; optional): The pack a consumer should migrate to instead. `version` uses the same minimal-constraint grammar as the root `packs[]` array (exact or caret). |

## 1. Concept

A kind of record the app stores: its fields, lifecycle, invariants and who may read or write it. This section also holds everything that belongs to describing data: field types, reusable domain types, numbering sequences, first-boot seed rows, row and field level access, presentation hints and aggregates (a root concept that owns child collections read and saved as one unit).

### `concept`

A kind of record the app stores. A concept has fields, and optionally invariants, indexes, row-level access, events, a lifecycle (state machine), a composition (aggregate of child collections) and presentation hints. Each concept becomes a table, a REST resource and a generated screen.

**Used in:** `concepts` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The concept's name, unique within the model (PascalCase by convention). It names the table, the REST resource (`/api/<Concept>`) and every reference to the concept from queries, flows and screens. |
| `specializes` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a base concept (usually contributed by a pack, written `pack::Concept`) that this concept specializes: it starts from the base's fields, invariants and events and may add to them. The base is pinned to the pack version the app was generated against (see `specializesFloat`). |
| `specializesFloat` | `boolean` | optional | When this concept specializes a pack-contributed base, the parent is pinned by default to the pack version this app was last generated against -- generation refuses once the pack has moved unless this is explicitly set to true, opting this concept into always tracking the pack's current version. Ignored when the base is not pack-contributed. |
| `truthLevel` | one of `T0`, `T1`, `T2`, `T3`, `T4`, `T5`, `T6` | optional | The concept's declared verification maturity, `T0` (least) to `T6` (most). The release gate (`--releaseGate --targetTruthLevel=<T>`) refuses to promote a model whose concepts are below the target level. |
| `module` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the bounded context (`modules[]` entry) this concept belongs to. Other contexts refer to it as `context::Concept`. |
| `renamedFrom` | `string` | optional | Declares this concept is a rename of a previously-existing concept with this name, so a regeneration's schema-lifecycle classifies its table as a rename instead of an unrelated drop+create. |
| `uid` | `string` (pattern `^[a-z0-9]{8,32}$`) | optional | A stable identity for this concept, generated once and never reused (npdev migrate assign-uids stamps one). When a live table's persisted uid matches a model concept's uid but the name differs, the rename is resolved by identity -- declared by construction, no renamedFrom needed. Optional: a model with no uids behaves exactly as before. |
| `satelliteOf` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Declares this concept is a satellite extension of a base concept owned by another pack (a pack-qualified reference, e.g. "identity::User"). The base pack stays untouched; this concept must also declare a unique+required `type: reference` field whose `reference.target` equals this value (the 1:1 anchor bond the satellite hangs off), enforced by SemanticValidator. |
| `softDelete` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | This concept's rows are never physically deleted. A generated delete flips a platform-managed `deletedAt` timestamp instead of removing the row; every generated read (list/page/aggregate/existsUnique/reference finder) excludes a row with `deletedAt` set, and a generated restore action clears it. A `unique:true` field (or compound-unique invariant) is enforced among live (non-deleted) rows only -- a value freed by a soft delete can be reused immediately. |
| `system` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | The platform owns this concept (for example the identity pack's Credential, which holds password hashes). A system concept gets NO generated REST route, menu entry, export/import, seed screen, agent/MCP tool or catalog listing; only platform code (the auth controllers) reads or writes it. Apps never declare one for credentials: the identity pack provides it, and a model concept carrying a password hash is a validation error. |
| `temporal` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | This concept carries effective-dated rows (price lists, tax rates, assignments -- multiple rows for the same logical entity, valid over different, non-overlapping windows). Requires the concept to also declare its own author-owned `validFrom`/`validTo` fields (type: date, required: true -- ordinary business fields, not platform-managed columns; a still-open-ended row uses a far-future sentinel date rather than a null validTo), enforced at compile time. The generic concept-CRUD read/list/query endpoint (`GET /api/concepts/{conceptName}`) accepts an `asOf=<date>` query parameter that composes with any other `where=` filter already supported there (e.g. `where=productCode:eq:P100&asOf=2026-03-15` resolves the row effective for that product on that date) -- `validFrom<=asOf<=validTo` is pushed down as two ordinary ConceptQuery filters, and a temporal concept's default view (asOf absent) resolves as of today, matching `softDelete`'s own default-excludes-noncurrent-rows convention. Scoping resolution to "the same logical entity" (e.g. the same product) is the caller's job via an ordinary `where=` filter, not a new identity-key schema concept -- deliberately deferred, see ledger RUN-22. |
| `collaboration` | object | optional | Record collaboration. `comments: true` gives every record of this concept a comment thread in its details view (plain text, `@username` mentions); `attachments: true` additionally lets files be attached to that thread. The thread is served by /api/records/{concept}/{id}/comments and is gated by the record's own read access: a caller who cannot read the row gets 404 for its comments, never a hint that it exists.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`comments` (`boolean`; optional; default `false`): Every record of this concept gets a comment thread.<br>`attachments` (`boolean`; optional; default `false`): Files can be attached to the record's thread (requires comments: true). |
| `rollups` | array of object | optional | STORED fields of this concept the platform keeps equal to an aggregate over a child concept's rows -- e.g. Mosaic.likeCount = count of Like rows whose mosaicId points at it. Recomputed inside every child save/delete/restore (and on every save of this concept, so a client can never write the value itself), without bumping this row's version, so the value is an ordinary sortable/filterable column. field: a numeric field of this concept; from: the child concept; via: the child's reference field to this concept; fn: count (default) \| sum \| min \| max \| avg; of: the child's numeric field the non-count functions read.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`field` (`string`; required; min length 1): The stored field of this concept that holds the aggregate.<br>`from` (`string`; required; min length 1): The child concept whose rows are aggregated.<br>`via` (`string`; required; min length 1): The field of the child concept that points at this concept.<br>`fn` (one of `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `avg`; optional): The aggregate function: count (default), sum, min, max or avg.<br>`of` (`string`; optional; min length 1): The child field the function applies to (not used by `count`). |
| `fields` | array of [`field`](#field) (min items 1) | required | The concept's fields, at least one. Field order is the default display order. |
| `invariants` | array of [`invariant`](#invariant) | optional | Rules every row must satisfy (uniqueness or boolean expressions). A violation rejects the write. |
| `indexes` | array of [`index`](#index) | optional | Extra database indexes (the platform already indexes ids and unique fields). |
| `access` | [`conceptAccess`](#conceptaccess) | optional | Row-level read and write rules, and an optional anonymous public read grant, for this concept. |
| `events` | array of [`event`](#event) | optional | Events declared inside the concept. A nested event with `mode` is published automatically by the generated create, update or delete. |
| `lifecycle` | [`lifecycle`](#lifecycle) | optional | The concept's state machine: status field, states and allowed transitions. |
| `composition` | [`composition`](#composition) | optional | Makes the concept the root of an aggregate whose child collections are read and saved whole. |
| `ui` | [`presentationMetadata`](#presentationmetadata) | optional | Presentation hints for the concept as a whole (labels, form layout, default grouping, offline writes). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "Invoice",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "uuid",
      "id": true
    },
    {
      "name": "number",
      "type": "string",
      "required": true,
      "unique": true,
      "defaultExpression": "nextNumber('invoice')"
    },
    {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "decimal",
      "precision": 12,
      "scale": 2,
      "min": 0
    }
  ],
  "softDelete": true
}
```

### `field`

One column of a concept (and one entry of an object's properties). The `type` decides the stored shape; the remaining keywords add constraints, defaults, references, enum members and presentation.

**Used in:** `concept.fields`

**Conditional rules:**

- When `type` is `enum` and `type` is present: requires at least one of `enumValues`, `values`.
- When `type` is `object` and `type` is present: requires `properties`.
- When `type` is `array` and `type` is present: requires `items`; each `items` entry has `type` one of `object`, `enum`.
- When `type` is `reference` and `type` is present: requires at least one of `ref`, `reference`.
- When `type` is `file` and `type` is present: `unique` must be `false`; `reference` is not allowed; `ref` is not allowed.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The field's name: its column name and its JSON key in the REST API. Unique within the concept. |
| `type` | one of `string`, `uuid`, `int`, `integer`, `long`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum`, `reference`, `object`, `array`, `file` | optional | The stored type. `string`, `uuid`, `int` / `integer` (32-bit), `long` (64-bit), `decimal` (use with `precision` and `scale`), `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum` (needs `enumValues`), `reference` (to another concept's row), `object` (structured, described by `properties`), `array` (described by `items`), `file` (an uploaded file handle). |
| `id` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | When true this field is the concept's identifier (primary key). Conventionally a `uuid` field named `id`. |
| `required` | `boolean` or array of `string` | optional | True: a value must be supplied on create and may not be cleared. On an `object` field this may instead be a list of the property names that are required inside the object. |
| `unique` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | True: no two rows (within one tenant, and among non-deleted rows when the concept uses `softDelete`) may hold the same value. |
| `sensitive` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | Marks the field as sensitive. It is redacted before it can appear in any external-AI review pack, by field name across all concepts (it deliberately over-redacts rather than risk missing one). At runtime a sensitive field with no `access.read` rule of its own is omitted from every generated read, list and query response for every caller (administrators included), is never offered to agent tools or search, and is redacted in audit trails. Declaring `access.read` on the field is the explicit grant that returns it to whoever passes the rule. |
| `connectable` | one of `anchor` | optional | Set to `anchor` on a unique, non-id field to make it a natural-key anchor that other concepts may reference with `reference.via` (the foreign key then points at this field, scoped by tenant). |
| `renamedFrom` | `string` | optional | Declares this field is a rename of a previously-existing column with this name, so a regeneration's schema-lifecycle classifies it as a rename instead of an unrelated remove+add. |
| `uid` | `string` (pattern `^[a-z0-9]{8,32}$`) | optional | A stable identity for this field, generated once and never reused (npdev migrate assign-uids stamps one). When a live column's persisted uid matches a model field's uid but the name differs, the rename is resolved by identity -- declared by construction, no renamedFrom needed. Optional: a model with no uids behaves exactly as before. |
| `picker` | object | optional | Declares a filter/multiSelect for this field's auto-picker (a reference field's browse/pick dialog). Same two properties a band's bandPickers entry accepts -- one picker shape for both surfaces.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`filter` (`string`; optional; min length 1): An AND-composed predicate (`field == literal && field == literal`) constraining the picker's candidate rows; a literal may be `$root.<field>`, the aggregate's root record (or, with no enclosing aggregate, the field's own record). Enforced server-side. OR is not supported; use a `visibleWhen` predicate instead.<br>`multiSelect` (`boolean`; optional; default `false`): True lets the user pick several rows.<br>`selectorRef` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Name of a `screens` entry of kind `picker` whose columns, filters, order and `where` are adopted wholesale. This picker's own `filter`, if also given, is combined with the picker screen's using AND. |
| `access` | object | optional | field-level (not row-level) authorization -- the next rung on the ladder below concept.access: role ceiling (permission) -&gt; row scope (concept.access) -&gt; field scope (this). Each expression is evaluated per-record through the platform's unified expression language (ComputedExpression), with $user.id/$user.tenantId/$user.actorId/$user.roles available alongside the record's own fields, exactly like concept.access. read gates whether this field's value may appear in a read/list/query response for a given record (denied means the field key is OMITTED from the response, never returned masked/null). write gates whether a save may set/change this field's value (denied means the WHOLE write is rejected, never silently dropped). Absent = no additional field-level restriction beyond the concept's own row-level access and role permissions.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`read` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Expression evaluated per record; while false the field is hidden from the caller.<br>`write` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Expression evaluated per record; while false the field is read-only for the caller. |
| `file` | object | optional | Metadata for a file-typed field. The persisted value is a FileHandle (or list, if multiple), never raw bytes.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`contentTypes` (array of `string`; optional; min items 1): Allowed MIME types of the uploaded file.<br>`maxSizeBytes` (`integer`; optional; min 1): Largest allowed upload in bytes.<br>`multiple` (`boolean`; optional; default `false`): True: the field holds a list of files. |
| `enumValues` | array of `string` or [`enumOption`](#enumoption) (min items 1) | optional | The allowed values of an `enum` field, in display order. Each entry is a plain string or an `enumOption` object that adds a label, icon, badge or order. |
| `values` | array of `string` or [`enumOption`](#enumoption) (min items 1) | optional | Alias of `enumValues`. |
| `ref` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Shorthand for the target of a reference field: the name of the referenced concept. Prefer `reference`. |
| `reference` | `string` or [`referenceDefinition`](#referencedefinition) | optional | Makes the field a reference to another concept's row. Either the target concept's name, or a `referenceDefinition` object that also configures lookup, preview and delete behavior. |
| `domainType` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a `domainTypes[]` entry whose base type, validation, normalization and presentation this field inherits. |
| `description` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A sentence saying what the field holds. Shown as help in the generated UI and read by AI authors. |
| `default` | any value | optional | A literal value stored when the caller does not supply one on create. |
| `defaultExpression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | An expression evaluated on create when the caller supplies no value, for example `nextNumber('invoice')`, `today()` or `$user.id`. Not re-applied on update. |
| `derivedExpression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | An expression that computes the field's value from the row's other fields. The value is calculated by the platform, not supplied by clients. |
| `minLength` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Minimum number of characters of a `string` value. |
| `maxLength` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Maximum number of characters of a `string` value. |
| `min` | `number` | optional | Smallest allowed numeric value (inclusive) for `int`, `long` and `decimal` fields. |
| `max` | `number` | optional | Largest allowed numeric value (inclusive) for `int`, `long` and `decimal` fields. |
| `precision` | `integer` (min 1; max 38) | optional | Total number of digits of a `decimal` field (1 to 38). |
| `scale` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Number of digits after the decimal point of a `decimal` field. |
| `minItems` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Minimum number of elements of an `array` field. |
| `maxItems` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Maximum number of elements of an `array` field. |
| `uniqueItems` | `boolean` | optional | True: the elements of an `array` field must all be different. |
| `itemIdentityField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For an `array` of objects, the property of each element that identifies it; used together with `duplicationPolicy` to detect duplicates. |
| `duplicationPolicy` | one of `allow`, `deny` | optional | For an `array` field: `allow` or `deny` elements that share the same identity (`itemIdentityField`). |
| `properties` | map of name to [`schemaObject`](#schemaobject) | optional | For an `object` field, the structure: a map from property name to a `schemaObject` describing that property. |
| `items` | [`schemaObject`](#schemaobject) | optional | For an `array` field, the `schemaObject` describing every element. |
| `ui` | [`uiField`](#uifield) | optional | Presentation hints for this one field (label, placeholder, widget, grouping, visibility rules). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "status",
  "type": "enum",
  "required": true,
  "enumValues": [
    "OPEN",
    "PAID"
  ],
  "default": "OPEN"
}
```

### `fieldConvention`

A field naming convention: a concept field that declares no `type` takes the defaults of the first rule matching its name. `match` is an exact field name ("name") or a camelCase ending ("*Name": the LAST camelCase word is Name -- clientName matches, hasToRename and name do not). An exact match beats an ending, a longer ending beats a shorter one, equals keep the earlier rule (model rules, then pack rules, then the built-in conventions-basic: name, *Name = string(50), *Dt = date, *Dtt = datetime; a model overrides a built-in rule by declaring the same `match`). A field that declares its own type is never touched; a field with no type that no rule matches is an error. The array is consumed at composition time and never reaches the compiled model.

**Used in:** `fieldConventions` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match` | `string` (pattern `^(\*[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\|[a-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$`) | required | Which field names the rule types: an exact name (`name`) or a camelCase ending (`*Dt`). An ending matches when the field's LAST camelCase word is that text, so `*Name` matches `clientName` and `shippingAddressName` but not `name` (that is an exact rule) and not `hasToRename`. An exact rule beats an ending, a longer ending beats a shorter one. |
| `defaults` | object | optional | What a matching field takes when it leaves the property out: always a `type`, optionally the size and constraint keys listed under it. A field that declares its own `type` is never touched.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`type` (one of `string`, `uuid`, `int`, `integer`, `long`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`; required): The field type the rule gives: string, uuid, int, integer, long, decimal, boolean, date or datetime.<br>`maxLength` (`integer`; optional; min 0): Longest text the field accepts; an explicit `maxLength` on the field wins.<br>`minLength` (`integer`; optional; min 0): Shortest text the field accepts.<br>`precision` (`integer`; optional; min 1; max 38): Total digits of a decimal field (1 to 38).<br>`scale` (`integer`; optional; min 0): Digits after the decimal point of a decimal field.<br>`min` (`number`; optional): Smallest value a number field accepts.<br>`max` (`number`; optional): Largest value a number field accepts.<br>`required` (`boolean`; optional): Whether the field must be present.<br>`unique` (`boolean`; optional): Whether no two rows may share the value.<br>`sensitive` (`boolean`; optional): Marks the field as sensitive (omitted from reads and logs unless granted). |

### `domainType`

A reusable, named field type (for example an email address or a postal code): a base type plus validation, normalization and presentation that every field using it inherits through `field.domainType`.

**Used in:** `domainTypes` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The domain type's name, referenced by `field.domainType`. |
| `baseType` | one of `string`, `uuid`, `int`, `integer`, `long`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime` | required | The stored type that fields of this domain type get (a scalar field type). |
| `validation` | [`schemaObject`](#schemaobject) | optional | A `schemaObject` with the constraints (length, range, pattern, ...) applied to every field of this type. |
| `normalization` | array of `string` | optional | Names of normalizations applied to a value before it is validated and stored (for example `trim`, `lowercase`). |
| `format` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A format hint for the value (for example an input mask or a well-known format name); also shown to users and AI authors. |
| `examples` | array of `string` | optional | Example values, used in generated help and in tests. |
| `ui` | [`uiField`](#uifield) | optional | Presentation hints inherited by every field of this type. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "Email",
  "baseType": "string",
  "validation": {
    "type": "string",
    "maxLength": 254,
    "regex": "^[^@\\s]+@[^@\\s]+$"
  },
  "normalization": [
    "trim",
    "lowercase"
  ]
}
```

### `enumOption`

A rich enum member, written instead of a plain string inside `field.enumValues` / `field.values` when the member needs a label, an icon, a badge or a position.

**Used in:** `field.enumValues`, `field.values`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The stored value of this enum member. |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | The text shown for the member (a plain string or per-locale object). |
| `displayLabel` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | An alternative display text used where the short `label` is not enough, for example in a form dropdown. |
| `order` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Position of the member in dropdowns and filters (lower first). Members without `order` follow in declaration order. |
| `group` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Heading under which the member is grouped in dropdowns. |
| `default` | `boolean` | optional | True: this member is preselected on create. |
| `deprecated` | `boolean` | optional | True: existing rows may keep the value but it is no longer offered for new data. |
| `icon` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Icon name shown next to the member. |
| `iconHint` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Accessible text explaining the icon. |
| `badge` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Short badge text or color token shown next to the member. |
| `badgeHint` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Accessible text explaining the badge. |
| `description` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A sentence describing what the member means. |
| `help` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Longer help shown when the user focuses the member. |

### `referenceDefinition`

The long form of `field.reference`: the target concept of a reference field plus how the generated UI looks it up, previews it and what happens on delete.

**Used in:** `field.reference`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The referenced concept's name (`Concept`, or `pack::Concept` / `context::Concept` for one declared elsewhere). |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | optional | True: the field holds a list of references instead of one. |
| `displayField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Field of the target used as the human-readable text of a reference. |
| `lookupFields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields of the target shown in lookup results. |
| `searchFields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields of the target the picker searches when the user types. |
| `previewFields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields of the target shown in the hover or detail preview of a selected reference. |
| `displayTemplate` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A template combining target fields into the displayed text, for example `{code} - {name}`. |
| `pickerColumns` | array of `string` | optional | Columns of the target shown in the picker dialog. |
| `previewCardTemplate` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A template for the preview card shown for a selected reference. |
| `defaultFilter` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A predicate that restricts which target rows the picker offers. |
| `defaultFilterBehavior` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Alias of `defaultFilter`. |
| `inlineCreate` | one of `allow`, `deny` | optional | `allow` lets the user create a new target row from inside the picker; `deny` hides that option. |
| `via` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a field of the target to reference instead of its id. It must be the target's id or a unique field marked `connectable: anchor`. |
| `onDelete` | one of `restrict`, `cascade`, `nullify` | optional | What happens to this field when the referenced row is deleted: `restrict` refuses the delete, `cascade` deletes the referencing rows too, `nullify` clears the reference. |

Example:

```json
{
  "target": "Customer",
  "displayField": "name",
  "searchFields": [
    "name",
    "email"
  ],
  "onDelete": "restrict"
}
```

### `schemaObject`

A small inline type description (a JSON-Schema-like subset) used wherever a value is not a concept field: object and array shapes of fields, a domain type's validation, capability operation inputs and outputs, a flow's input and output schema and a procedure's returns. It is recursive through `properties` and `items`.

**Used in:** `field.properties`, `field.items`, `domainType.validation`, `capabilityOperation.input`, `capabilityOperation.output`, `flow.inputSchema`, `flow.outputSchema`, `queryParameter.schema`, `schemaObject.properties`, `schemaObject.items`

**Conditional rules:**

- When `type` is `array`: requires `items`.
- When `type` is `object`: requires `properties`.
- When `enumValues` is present: `type` must be `"enum"`.
- When `values` is present: `type` must be `"enum"`.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | one of `object`, `array`, `string`, `uuid`, `int`, `integer`, `long`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `enum`, `reference` | optional | The value type: a scalar field type, `object`, `array` or `reference`. |
| `description` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A sentence describing the value. |
| `minLength` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Minimum length of a string. |
| `maxLength` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Maximum length of a string. |
| `min` | `number` | optional | Smallest allowed numeric value. |
| `max` | `number` | optional | Largest allowed numeric value. |
| `precision` | `integer` (min 1; max 38) | optional | Total digits of a decimal. |
| `scale` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Digits after the decimal point of a decimal. |
| `minItems` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Minimum number of elements of an array. |
| `maxItems` | `integer` (min 0) | optional | Maximum number of elements of an array. |
| `uniqueItems` | `boolean` | optional | True: array elements must all be different. |
| `itemIdentityField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Property that identifies an array element, used with `duplicationPolicy`. |
| `duplicationPolicy` | one of `allow`, `deny` | optional | `allow` or `deny` array elements that share the same identity. |
| `regex` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A regular expression a string value must match. |
| `pattern` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Alias of `regex`. |
| `enumValues` | array of `string` (min items 1) | optional | The allowed values of an enum value. |
| `values` | array of `string` (min items 1) | optional | Alias of `enumValues`. |
| `enum` | array of `string` (min items 1) | optional | Alias of `enumValues`. |
| `required` | array of `string` | optional | For an object, the names of the properties that must be present. |
| `properties` | map of name to [`schemaObject`](#schemaobject) | optional | For an object, a map from property name to the `schemaObject` describing it. |
| `items` | [`schemaObject`](#schemaobject) | optional | For an array, the `schemaObject` describing every element. |
| `default` | any value | optional | A literal default value. |
| `defaultExpression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | An expression giving the default value when none is supplied. |
| `derivedExpression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | An expression that computes the value from its siblings. |

### `localizableLabel`

A text shown to users. Either a plain string, or an object with a required `default` text plus one entry per locale (for example `pt-BR`); the runtime picks the requested locale, then its language, then `default`.

**Used in:** `property.label`, `workbenchAction.label`, `workbenchBandPicker.label`, `transactionDerivedField.label`, `transactionUiState.label`, `lifecycleState.label`, `lifecycleTransition.actionLabel`, `enumOption.label`, `enumOption.displayLabel`, `presentationMetadata.label`, `presentationMetadata.shortLabel`, `actionMetadata.label`, `panelAction.label`, `documentBand.label`

Accepted forms:

- `string`
- an object. Keys written inside it: `default` (`string`; required; min length 1): The text used when the requested locale and its language have no entry. Other keys are locale tags such as `pt-BR`.

### `presentationMetadata`

Presentation hints for the generated UI. Used on a concept (`concept.ui`: whole-list and whole-form behavior) and on a field (`field.ui`, `domainType.ui`, a panel field binding's `ui`: how the one field is labelled, grouped and edited). Hints only change how data is shown; they never widen access or change what is stored.

**Used in:** `concept.ui`, `panelFieldBinding.ui`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | The user-facing name of the field or concept (plain string or per-locale object). Defaults to a prettified name. |
| `shortLabel` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | A shorter name used where space is tight, such as a table header or a mobile card. |
| `description` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A sentence of help shown next to the control. |
| `placeholder` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Hint text shown inside an empty input. |
| `helpText` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Longer help text shown under the control. |
| `order` | `integer` | optional | Position of the field in forms and details (lower first). |
| `widget` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The control used to edit the field (for example `text`, `textarea`, `select`, `checkbox`, `date`, `number`, `custom`). It must be compatible with the field's type; the validator checks it. With `custom`, `customWidgetRef` names the component. |
| `group` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the group the field belongs to in a form; fields with the same group render together. |
| `section` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the form section (a titled block) the field is placed in. |
| `advanced` | `boolean` | optional | True: the field is tucked away under an Advanced toggle. |
| `deprecated` | `boolean` | optional | True: the field is kept for old data but hidden for new entries. |
| `examples` | array of `string` | optional | Example values shown as hints. |
| `visibleWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression over the record; the control is shown only while it is true. |
| `enabledWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression over the record; the control is editable only while it is true. |
| `readonlyWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression over the record; while true the control is read-only. |
| `requiredWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression over the record; while true the control is marked and enforced as required. |
| `pickerType` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | How a reference field is picked, for example a `search-dialog`. |
| `allowInlineCreate` | `boolean` | optional | True: the picker lets the user create a new target row in place. |
| `searchFields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields searched by the picker for this reference field. |
| `filterPreset` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a preset filter applied to the picker's candidate rows. |
| `tab` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the form tab the field is placed on. |
| `column` | `integer` | optional | Grid column (1-based) the field occupies in a multi-column form. |
| `columnSpan` | `integer` | optional | Number of grid columns the field spans in a multi-column form. |
| `width` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Preferred width of the field's control or column (a CSS size or a keyword). |
| `summaryCard` | `boolean` | optional | True: the field is shown on the record's summary card. |
| `listColumn` | `boolean` | optional | True: the field is a column of the list; false hides it from the list. |
| `showInDefaultWebUi` | `boolean` | optional | False hides the field from the generated web UI entirely (it stays in the API). |
| `listColumnOrder` | `integer` | optional | Position of the field among the list columns (lower first). |
| `formColumns` | `integer` | optional | Concept-level. Number of columns of the create and edit form (default 1). |
| `displayMode` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Concept-level. How the concept's records are shown by default, for example `standard`. |
| `formPresentation` | one of `modal`, `standard` | optional | Concept-level. `standard` (default) opens the create and edit form in place of the list with a Back to list action; `modal` opens it as a popup dialog. |
| `defaultSort` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Concept-level. The field the list is sorted by by default. |
| `defaultGroup` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Concept-level. An `enum` field whose members become the columns of the generated board (kanban) view; defaults to the lifecycle status field. |
| `imageField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | On a reference field or concept: the field of the target that holds an image, shown as the thumbnail of a selected reference. |
| `customWidgetRef` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | With `widget: custom`: the relative path of the app-supplied widget component that renders the field. |
| `currency` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | ISO currency code (for example `BRL`) used to format a numeric field as money. |
| `offlineWrite` | `boolean` | optional | concept-level only. The generated UI may queue creates and updates of this concept while the device is offline and replay them on reconnect, showing them as pending sync. A queued update carries the version it was edited from; if the row changed meanwhile the server refuses it and the UI keeps it for the user to redo (reject policy, never a silent overwrite). Off unless declared; ignored on a field. |
| `selectionTools` | `boolean` | optional | Concept-level only. The generated list grid (table or grid of records) offers three tools on the rows the user has ticked: open them together in one dialog, copy them to the clipboard as spreadsheet cells, and download them as one merged CSV file. The per-row checkbox, select-all / deselect-all and the existing bulk delete and set-field actions are unaffected. On unless declared false: set false on a concept to hide the three tools on its grid; the manifest carries the key only then. Ignored on a field. |

Example:

```json
{
  "label": "Customer",
  "formColumns": 2,
  "defaultGroup": "status",
  "formPresentation": "modal"
}
```

### `uiField`

The `ui` of a field or domain type: an alias of presentationMetadata.

**Used in:** `field.ui`, `domainType.ui`

No keywords of its own; it is a plain value (see the tables that reference it).

### `conceptAccess`

Row-level authorization of a concept, evaluated per record: which rows a caller may read and which it may write, plus an optional anonymous public read grant.

**Used in:** `concept.access`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression evaluated per record that scopes which rows a caller may read; `$user.id`, `$user.tenantId`, `$user.roles` and the row's own fields are available. A row for which it is false is invisible. |
| `write` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression evaluated per record that scopes which rows a caller may change or delete. |
| `public` | object | optional | An anonymous, read-only grant served only by the RuntimeHost /api/public/** surface (GET only; writes are never public). where narrows which rows are public (the queries[].where grammar; must not reference $user -- there is no caller); absent means every row. fields is the explicit allow-list of fields served (id is always included). scope concept (default) gives the concept its own public list/get routes; scope aggregate serves it only as a child collection inside a public aggregate root.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`where` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Filter narrowing which rows are public (the query `where` grammar; it cannot use `$user`). Absent means every row.<br>`fields` (array of `string`; required; min items 1): The allow-list of fields served publicly (the id is always included).<br>`scope` (one of `concept`, `aggregate`; optional): `concept` (default): the concept is publicly readable on its own. `aggregate`: its aggregate is served as a whole. |

Example:

```json
{
  "read": "ownerId == $user.id || 'Manager' in $user.roles",
  "write": "ownerId == $user.id"
}
```

### `index`

A database index over one or more fields of a concept, optionally unique.

**Used in:** `concept.indexes`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the database index. Generated from the concept and fields when omitted. |
| `fields` | array of `string` (min items 1) | required | The fields the index covers, in order. At least one. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | optional | True: the combination of the indexed fields must be unique. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "ux_invoice_number",
  "fields": [
    "number"
  ],
  "unique": true
}
```

### `invariant`

A rule every row of the concept must satisfy before it is written. Either a uniqueness rule over fields (`type: unique`) or a boolean expression over the row (`type: expression`). A specializing concept can replace an inherited invariant with `override: true`.

**Used in:** `concept.invariants`

**Conditional rules:**

- At least one of `type`, `rule`, `expr`, `expression` must be present.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The rule's name, shown in the error when it is violated and used to refer to it from `override`. |
| `type` | one of `unique`, `expression` | optional | `unique` (the `fields` must be unique together) or `expression` (a boolean expression that must hold). |
| `specializes` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of an inherited invariant this one refines. |
| `override` | `boolean` | optional | True: replaces the inherited invariant of the same name in a specializing concept. |
| `rule` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A one-line rule text that the parser turns into the `type`, `fields` and `expression` of the invariant. Prefer the explicit keys. |
| `expr` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Alias of `expression`. |
| `expression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The boolean expression over the row's fields that must be true for a write to be accepted. |
| `fields` | array of `string` | optional | For `type: unique`, the fields whose combined values must be unique. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "PositiveTotal",
  "type": "expression",
  "expression": "total >= 0"
}
```

### `lifecycle`

The state machine of a concept: which field holds the state, the declared states and the allowed transitions between them.

**Used in:** `concept.lifecycle`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `statusField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The enum field that stores the current state. Defaults to a field named `status`. |
| `states` | array of [`lifecycleState`](#lifecyclestate) | optional | The declared states, with labels, initial and terminal marks. When omitted they are derived from the transitions. |
| `transitions` | array of [`lifecycleTransition`](#lifecycletransition) (min items 1) | required | The allowed moves between states, at least one. A move not listed here is refused. |

Example:

```json
{
  "statusField": "status",
  "states": [
    {
      "value": "OPEN",
      "initial": true
    },
    {
      "value": "PAID",
      "terminal": true
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    {
      "from": "OPEN",
      "to": "PAID",
      "event": "Pay"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `lifecycleState`

One state of a lifecycle.

**Used in:** `lifecycle.states`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The state's stored value (a member of the status field). |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | The text shown for the state. |
| `initial` | `boolean` | optional | True: new rows start in this state. |
| `terminal` | `boolean` | optional | A final state. The validator refuses any transition that leaves it. The row is also read-only and the board column is marked terminal. |
| `allowedActions` | array of `string` | optional | Names of the actions offered while a row is in this state. |
| `metadata` | map of name to `string` | optional | Free-form string notes about the state, carried into the compiled model unchanged. |

### `lifecycleTransition`

One allowed move from a state to another, optionally guarded by an expression and tied to an event and a button.

**Used in:** `lifecycle.transitions`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The state the transition leaves. |
| `to` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The state the transition enters. |
| `event` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the event that triggers (and is published by) this transition. |
| `guard` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression over the row that must be true for the transition to be allowed. |
| `actionLabel` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the button that performs the transition. |
| `action` | [`actionMetadata`](#actionmetadata) | optional | Presentation of the transition's action (confirmation text, success message, danger level). |
| `requiredPayload` | array of `string` | optional | Names of fields of the row that must hold a value for the transition to be performed. |
| `requires` | array of `string` | optional | Alias of `requiredPayload`. |
| `metadata` | map of name to `string` | optional | Free-form string notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |

### `actionMetadata`

How an action button is presented: caption, confirmation text, success and failure messages, danger level and visibility. Used on a lifecycle transition, a flow and a flow step.

**Used in:** `lifecycleTransition.action`, `flow.action`, `flowStep.action`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the action button. |
| `confirmationText` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Question shown for confirmation before the action runs. |
| `successMessage` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Message shown after the action succeeds. |
| `failureHint` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Hint shown to the user when the action fails. |
| `dangerLevel` | one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | optional | How destructive the action is: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `critical`; higher levels get stronger confirmation styling. |
| `visibleWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the button is shown only while it is true. |
| `permissionHint` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Text explaining which permission the action needs. |
| `inputFormHint` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Free-text hint for how the action's input form should be rendered. It is parsed and exposed through the runtime UI metadata API but does not change rendering today; use it to document authoring intent. |

### `composition`

Turns a concept into the root of an aggregate: a header plus owned child collections that are read and saved whole, in one transaction, at `/api/v1/runtime/aggregate/<Concept>`. Also holds the cross-collection rules (invariants, balances) and the hooks that run around a commit.

**Used in:** `concept.composition`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collections` | array of [`aggregateCollection`](#aggregatecollection) | optional | The aggregate's child collections, each loaded and saved with the root. |
| `onCommit` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a procedure (or a flow of that name) that runs after the whole tree is written, in the same transaction; a failure rolls everything back. |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |
| `onValidate` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Names a procedure run BEFORE the root upsert, inside the same transaction as commit() -- a non-ok result aborts the whole commit with NO writes at all. A sibling of onCommit (which runs AFTER the tree is written, rolling back on failure), not a flag on it: different timing, different contract. |
| `invariants` | array of [`aggregateInvariant`](#aggregateinvariant) | optional | Declarative cross-collection invariants evaluated against the whole aggregate draft tree (root fields plus every named collection) in the SAME pre-commit transaction slot onValidate uses -- a veto names the failing rule in the commit API error. |
| `balances` | array of [`aggregateBalance`](#aggregatebalance) | optional | Declarative, grouped cross-collection balance rules -- a role-partitioned collection's quantities must sum equal per group (e.g. Origem vs Destino per product/validity). Evaluated as a commit-time gate (alongside invariants) and, on demand without persisting, by a workbenchAction declaring checkBalances instead of procedure. |

### `aggregateCollection`

One child collection of an aggregate: the concept it holds, the field that points back to the parent and, optionally, nested collections and read-only lookup columns.

**Used in:** `composition.collections`, `aggregateCollection.collections`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The collection's name; its address inside the aggregate (nested ones are addressed `parent.child`). |
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The concept whose rows make up the collection. |
| `childField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Field of the child concept that points back to the parent row. |
| `ownership` | one of `owned`, `referenced` | optional | `owned` (default): the aggregate creates and deletes the child rows. `referenced`: the rows exist independently and are only linked. |
| `orderBy` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Field the collection's rows are ordered by. |
| `collections` | array of [`aggregateCollection`](#aggregatecollection) | optional | Nested child collections (a second level, such as lines and their positions). |
| `lookupFields` | array of [`aggregateCollectionLookupField`](#aggregatecollectionlookupfield) | optional | read-only fields attached to every row of this collection at load time, sourced from a declared query's results rather than persisted (e.g. a live maximum-quantity bound). Excluded from the commit payload. |

### `aggregateCollectionLookupField`

A read-only column attached to every row of a collection when it loads, fetched from a declared query and joined in memory. Never persisted.

**Used in:** `aggregateCollection.lookupFields`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The field name this lookup's value is attached under on every loaded row. Never persisted. |
| `query` | `string` (min length 1) | required | A declared query, run once (unparameterized) when the collection loads. |
| `joinField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | A field present on both the query's result rows and this collection's rows -- results are joined to rows in memory by equality on this field (no runtime query parameter binding exists anywhere in the platform today, so this is a load-time join, not a per-row parameterized query). |
| `valueField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The field read off the matching query result row and attached under `name`. |

### `aggregateInvariant`

A named rule evaluated over the whole aggregate draft (root fields plus every collection) just before commit; a failure vetoes the commit and names the rule.

**Used in:** `composition.invariants`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The rule identifier a commit-time API error names when this invariant vetoes a commit. Required and must be unique within its aggregate. |
| `expression` | `string` (min length 1) | required | A boolean-shaped expression evaluated against the aggregate draft tree -- root fields directly by name, each declared collection by name as a list (e.g. lines.all(l =&gt; l.qty &gt; 0) && lines.sum(qty) &lt;= totalQty). |
| `message` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional override for the veto message; defaults to a message composed from name plus the evaluator's own failure detail. |

### `aggregateBalance`

A named balance rule over a collection whose rows are split into two sides by a discriminator field (for example origin and destination): per group, the summed quantities of the two sides must be equal, or the commit is vetoed.

**Used in:** `composition.balances`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The rule identifier a commit-time API error names when this balance rule vetoes a commit. Required and must be unique within its aggregate. |
| `collection` | `string` (min length 1) | required | A dotted path into the aggregate's own composition tree naming the (possibly depth-2) collection this rule partitions, e.g. "itens.posicoes" -- the same address format aggregate.transaction.visibleWhen/regions already use. |
| `groupBy` | array of `string` | optional | Row field names partitioning the collection into balance groups (e.g. ["produtoId", "validade"]). Empty means one group for the whole collection. |
| `discriminatorField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The row field distinguishing the two sides of the balance (e.g. "papel"). |
| `leftValue` | `string` (min length 1) | required | discriminatorField value identifying the left side (e.g. "Origem"). |
| `rightValue` | `string` (min length 1) | required | discriminatorField value identifying the right side (e.g. "Destino"). Must differ from leftValue. |
| `quantityField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The numeric row field summed per side per group. |
| `message` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional business-language template for a per-group shortfall, e.g. "Faltam {delta} unidade(s) de {produtoId}" -- {delta} plus every groupBy field name are available as substitution tokens. Defaults to a message composed from name plus the computed delta. |

### `sequence`

A document-numbering counter such as INV-2026-0001. A field takes the next value with `defaultExpression: "nextNumber('<name>')"`.

**Used in:** `sequences` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (pattern `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`) | required | Identifier referenced by nextNumber('name') in a field's defaultExpression. Deliberately NOT namespace-qualified by pack composition -- same reasoning as this schema's webhook $def applies to source. |
| `format` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Render template for an allocated number. Recognized tokens: {seq} / {seq:N} (the running counter, zero-padded to N digits -- exactly one required), plus optional {year}/{yy}/{month}/{day} date tokens resolved at allocation time. Example: "INV-{year}-{seq:4}" -&gt; INV-2026-0001. Any date token also partitions the underlying counter, so numbering resets exactly when the rendered text would otherwise repeat. |
| `scope` | one of `global`, `tenant` | optional | Global (default): one counter shared by every tenant. tenant: one independent counter per tenant. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "invoice",
  "format": "INV-{year}-{seq:4}",
  "scope": "tenant"
}
```

### `seed`

Rows inserted once, automatically, at first boot through the same governed save path as any other write. A seed is one record, or many (`count` / `repeatOver`).

**Used in:** `seeds` (model root and pack file)

**Conditional rules:**

- Bulk-generated (repeatOver) rows can't be individually aliased.
- Bulk-generated (count) rows can't be individually aliased.
- repeatOver and count are two alternative bulk-generation mechanisms -- use only one.
- When `repeatOver` is present or `count` is present: requires `data`.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Concept this seed row targets. For a pack/context-declared seed, must name a concept the SAME pack/context declares (compile error otherwise, thrown at pack-composition time) -- rewritten to its pack-qualified form there. A root-declared seed may name any of the model's own concepts, unrestricted, exactly like a root-declared query or panel. |
| `alias` | `string` (pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$`) | optional | Optional local name a LATER seed record (anywhere in the fully resolved model) can reference via "$ref:&lt;alias&gt;". Only single (non-bulk) records may carry one -- must be unique across every declared seed. |
| `id` | `string` | optional | Explicit id for this record; a generated UUID is used at seed-run time when absent. |
| `data` | object | optional | Field values, same shape as a POST /api/&lt;concept&gt; body.
