| `uid` | `string` (pattern `^[a-z0-9]{8,32}$`) | optional | A stable identity for this panel, generated once and never reused (npdev migrate assign-uids stamps one). When a live element's persisted uid matches a model panel's uid but the name differs, the rename is resolved by identity -- declared by construction, no renamedFrom needed. Optional: a model with no uids behaves exactly as before. |
| `route` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The URL segment the panel is served at. |
| `title` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Heading of the panel. |
| `dataSources` | array of [`panelDataSource`](#paneldatasource) | optional | The row sources of the panel. |
| `layout` | [`panelLayout`](#panellayout) | optional | How the data sources are laid out. |
| `fieldBindings` | array of [`panelFieldBinding`](#panelfieldbinding) | optional | Binds fields of the data sources to the panel, with rules and hints. |
| `visibility` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the panel is visible only while it is true. |
| `enabledWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the panel is interactive only while it is true. |
| `actions` | array of [`panelAction`](#panelaction) | optional | The buttons of the panel. |
| `explainability` | object | optional | Free-form object describing, for AI and audit tools, why the panel exists and what it shows. |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`untrustedExtensionEntrypoint` (`string`; optional; min length 1): This panel's implementation is an author-supplied, hash-pinned untrusted extension (a relative path into the sibling untrusted-extension-manifest.json) rather than a normal DSL-declared body -- admitted through the same bytecode/AST safety gate as a mounted plugin. 'Untrusted' names the safety posture the platform treats it with, not a judgement on the author. |
| `guidePage` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the back-office guide page (dashboard) that hosts this panel. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "OrdersPanel",
  "route": "orders",
  "title": "Orders",
  "dataSources": [
    {
      "name": "orders",
      "concept": "Order"
    }
  ],
  "layout": {
    "type": "table"
  }
}
```

### `panelDataSource`

A source of rows for a panel: a concept, a query or a procedure, optionally nested under a parent data source.

**Used in:** `panel.dataSources`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The data source's name, referenced by field bindings, widgets and row actions. |
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Read rows of this concept. |
| `query` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Read rows from this query. |
| `procedure` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Replace the row source entirely with the output of this procedure (or a flow of that name). |
| `params` | object | optional | Binds the query's or procedure's parameters: a map from name to a literal or an expression. |
| `parentDataSource` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the data source this one is nested under (a master-detail relation). |
| `parentField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Field of the parent row that links to the child rows. |
| `childField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Field of this data source's rows that holds the parent link. |
| `rowOps` | array of one of `add`, `delete` (items one of `add`, `delete`) | optional | The row operations the user may do on this nested data source: `add` and/or `delete`. |
| `addFormFields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields shown in the form that adds a row. |
| `onRowLoad` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A procedure that ENRICHES the rows this data source produced -- adds fields, never reorders/adds/drops rows (a count or id mismatch is a hard runtime failure, not silent truncation). Distinct from `procedure` above, which REPLACES the row source entirely. |
| `totalField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Names a numeric field of this dataSource's own rows (as already scoped by fieldBindings' source prefix) to sum client-side across every currently-rendered row and display as a table footer -- e.g. a running quantity total for an item-wizard-style nested dataSource. Purely a display aggregate over already-loaded rows; never sent to the server, never affects the commit payload. |

### `panelLayout`

How a panel is laid out: a table or grid of its data sources, or a console or dashboard of declarative widgets; children nest layouts.

**Used in:** `panel.layout`, `panelLayout.children`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | one of `table`, `grid`, `console`, `dashboard` | required | Table (default) and grid render the data sources; console and dashboard render the declarative widgets[] instead. |
| `children` | array of [`panelLayout`](#panellayout) | optional | Nested layouts, laid out inside this one. |
| `fields` | array of `string` | optional | The fields shown by this layout, in order. |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |
| `slots` | array of [`panelSlot`](#panelslot) | optional | Hand-authored regions inside this generated panel. Each slot mounts an app-owned component (`web/regions/<component>.js`, registered with `window.npdev.regions.register`) above, below or in place of the generated body, and is handed the panel's live data through a narrowed API (panel, data, refresh, invoke). |
| `widgets` | array of [`panelWidget`](#panelwidget) | optional | The declarative widgets of a console or dashboard layout, computed client-side over the panel's own data sources (tile, chart, actions, history, table). |

### `panelWidget`

A declarative widget of a console or dashboard panel layout, computed in the browser over the panel's own data sources.

**Used in:** `panelLayout.widgets`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `tile`, `chart`, `actions`, `history`, `table` | required | Tile: one aggregate number. chart: an aggregate per groupBy value, drawn as bar/line/donut. actions: the panel's action bar (at most one). history: this session's action runs (at most one). table: a data source's rows. |
| `title` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Heading of the widget. |
| `dataSource` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of one of this panel's dataSources. Required for tile, chart and table. |
| `aggregate` | one of `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max` | optional | How a tile or chart reduces rows (default count). Everything except count needs field. |
| `field` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The numeric field that sum/avg/min/max reduce. |
| `groupBy` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Chart only: the field whose distinct values become the categories. |
| `chart` | one of `bar`, `line`, `donut` | optional | Chart only: how the categories are drawn. |
| `filter` | object | optional | Only rows whose field equals the given text are aggregated.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`field` (`string`; required; min length 1): Field of the data source to compare.<br>`equals` (`string`; required): Only rows whose field equals this text are aggregated. |
| `span` | `integer` (min 1; max 4) | optional | Width in a 4-column grid (default 1). |

### `panelSlot`

A hand-authored region inside a generated panel: an app-owned component mounted above, below or in place of the generated body.

**Used in:** `panelLayout.slots`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `placement` | one of `above`, `below`, `replace` | required | above/below: mounted before/after the generated body. replace: mounted instead of the generated body (at most one per panel). |
| `component` | `string` (pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`) | required | Name registered via window.npdev.regions.register(name, {mount, update, unmount}) in the app's own web/regions/&lt;name&gt;.js. |
| `label` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional heading shown above the mounted component. |

### `panelFieldBinding`

Binds a field of a data source to the panel's form or table, with visibility and editability rules and presentation hints. Also used by document bands.

**Used in:** `panel.fieldBindings`, `documentBand.fields`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The field being bound. |
| `source` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of the data source the field comes from (defaults to the panel's primary one). |
| `visibleWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the field is shown only while it is true. |
| `enabledWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the field is editable only while it is true. |
| `readonlyWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; while true the field is read-only. |
| `ui` | [`presentationMetadata`](#presentationmetadata) | optional | Presentation hints for this binding. |
| `editable` | `boolean` | optional | True: the user may edit the field in the panel. |

### `panelAction`

A button of a panel. It runs a query, a concept mutation, a procedure or a flow.

**Used in:** `panel.actions`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The action's name, unique within the panel. |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the button. |
| `binding` | one of `conceptQuery`, `conceptMutation`, `procedure`, `flow` | required | What the button does: run a `conceptQuery`, a `conceptMutation`, a `procedure` or a `flow`. |
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For a concept binding: the concept. |
| `operation` | one of `query`, `create`, `update`, `delete` | optional | For `conceptQuery` / `conceptMutation`: `query`, `create`, `update` or `delete`. |
| `procedure` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For a `procedure` binding: the procedure (or flow of that name) to run. |
| `flow` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For a `flow` binding: the flow to start. |
| `visibleWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the button is shown only while it is true. |
| `enabledWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Expression; the button is clickable only while it is true. |
| `permissionRequirements` | array of `string` | optional | Permissions the user must hold to see and run the action. |
| `explainability` | object | optional | Free-form object describing why the action exists, for AI and audit tools. |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |
| `scope` | one of `panel`, `row` (default `"panel"`) | optional | Panel: rendered once, no row context. row: rendered per row of dataSource, invoked with that row's id. |
| `dataSource` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Required when scope is row -- names the panel dataSource whose rows this action is rendered against. |
| `inputFields` | array of `string` | optional | Field names collected from the user before invoking this action, then passed as the flow/procedure input. Same declaration shape as panelDataSource.addFormFields. |
| `resultAs` | one of `download` | optional | Only valid on a procedure-binding action. When 'download', PanelRuntime.executeAction returns the procedure's return value as a real file download (Content-Disposition: attachment) instead of a JSON result -- requires filename and contentType. |
| `filename` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Required with resultAs: download -- the filename offered in the Content-Disposition header. |
| `contentType` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Required with resultAs: download -- the MIME type served in the Content-Type header, e.g. text/csv. |

### `autoPanel`

A panel generated from a concept or an aggregate: up to four surfaces (selection, detail, transaction, prompt) are synthesized and each can be tuned or replaced. The older way; new models use `screens`.

**Used in:** `autoPanels` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The panel's name. Defaults to one derived from the concept or aggregate. |
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The concept the panel is generated for. Give `concept` or `aggregate`. |
| `aggregate` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The aggregate root concept the panel is generated for (opens the aggregate workbench). |
| `route` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The URL segment the panel is served at. |
| `surfaces` | array of one of `selection`, `detail`, `transaction`, `prompt` (items one of `selection`, `detail`, `transaction`, `prompt`) | optional | Which surfaces to generate: `selection`, `detail`, `transaction`, `prompt`. Defaults to the usual ones for the kind of panel. |
| `selection` | [`autoPanelSurface`](#autopanelsurface) | optional | Settings of the selection surface (the list of rows). |
| `detail` | [`autoPanelSurface`](#autopanelsurface) | optional | Settings of the detail surface (one record). |
| `transaction` | [`autoPanelSurface`](#autopanelsurface) | optional | Settings of the transaction surface (the aggregate workbench). |
| `prompt` | [`autoPanelSurface`](#autopanelsurface) | optional | Settings of the prompt surface (a row picker used by other surfaces). |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |

### `autoPanelSurface`

One generated surface of an auto panel. A surface keyword is used only by the surface kinds it makes sense for (for example `layout` and `dataSource` on selection, `regions` and `actions` on the aggregate workbench transaction).

**Used in:** `autoPanel.selection`, `autoPanel.detail`, `autoPanel.transaction`, `autoPanel.prompt`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filters` | array of `string` | optional | Fields the user can filter by on this surface. |
| `columns` | array of `string` | optional | Columns shown on this surface, in order. |
| `fields` | array of `string` | optional | Fields shown on this surface, in order. |
| `computed` | array of object | optional | Extra read-only columns computed live from an expression.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`col` (`string`; required; min length 1): Name of the computed column.<br>`expr` (`string`; required; min length 1): The expression computing the column.<br>`collection` (`string`; optional; min length 1): On an aggregate-bound transaction, the section (itens), band (itens.posicoes) or sub-band whose rows this column is computed for. The expression sees the row's fields and $root.&lt;headerField&gt;, and is evaluated live in the browser as a read-only extra column. |
| `labelField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Field used as the display text of a row (for a prompt or selection). |
| `hooks` | [`transactionHooks`](#transactionhooks) | optional | Hooks around the workbench transaction. |
| `derivedFields` | map of name to [`transactionDerivedField`](#transactionderivedfield) | optional | display-only values recomputed from the current Aggregate Workbench draft, keyed by field name. Retires the untyped transaction.metadata.derived list. |
| `regions` | map of name to [`regionMount`](#regionmount) | optional | How an addressable region of the Aggregate Workbench is filled, keyed by the region's address DERIVED from the aggregate's own composition tree (e.g. "itens", "itens.posicoes"; "header" for the root header region) -- addresses are never authored, only referenced here. A region absent from this map renders generated (the platform default). |
| `actions` | array of [`workbenchAction`](#workbenchaction) | optional | Typed replacement for transaction.metadata.actions. A typo'd key here now fails at schema time. |
| `visibleWhen` | map of name to `string` | optional | Typed predicates that show or hide a region of the aggregate workbench, keyed by collection or band name (for example `"itens": "$root.tipo != 'CANCELLED'"`). Predicates may combine clauses with `&&` and `\|\|` and may read `$root.<field>` and `$ui.<name>`. Presentation only: a hidden collection's rows still commit unchanged, and this never gates persistence or authorization. |
| `uiState` | map of name to [`transactionUiState`](#transactionuistate) | optional | Declared transient UI state, keyed by name, that a $ui.&lt;name&gt; visibleWhen predicate on this surface can read. Presentation-only -- never part of the commit payload. |
| `bandPickers` | map of name to [`workbenchBandPicker`](#workbenchbandpicker) | optional | Modal row pickers for the bands (collections) of the aggregate workbench, keyed by band collection name. A picker may name a selection panel, or give only `filter` and `multiSelect` and use no panel. |
| `dataSource` | [`autoPanelDataSource`](#autopaneldatasource) | optional | Replaces the generated row source of a selection surface (see `autoPanelDataSource`). |
| `layout` | one of `table`, `grid` | optional | Selection surface only: the layout type of the generated Selection panel, which also lists rows on the workbench page. `grid` renders each row as a card (the selection columns, one line each); `table` is the default. |
| `panel` | `string` | optional | AutoPanel surface override: the name of a declared panel that REPLACES this surface's synthesized panel. The expander skips generating the surface and every reference to it (route, workbench wiring, Prompt picker) uses the declared panel instead; the other surfaces stay generated. The panel must exist and be bound to the same concept the surface would have used (the aggregate root for an aggregate-bound AutoPanel's selection/transaction). |
| `metadata` | object | optional | Free-form notes carried into the compiled model unchanged. |

### `autoPanelDataSource`

Replaces the rows of a selection surface with the output of a procedure instead of the concept's table.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.dataSource`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `procedure` | `string` (min length 1) | required | A declared procedure whose return value becomes this surface's rows. |

### `workbenchAction`

A button on the aggregate workbench. It either runs a procedure over the current draft or checks balance rules; exactly one of `procedure` or `checkBalances`, enforced by the semantic validator.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.actions`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `procedure` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Declared procedure this action invokes over the draft. Mutually exclusive with checkBalances. |
| `checkBalances` | array of `string` | optional | Names declared aggregate.balances[] rules to evaluate against the current draft and return as a report, WITHOUT invoking a procedure or persisting anything -- an on-demand "Recalcular Saldos" affordance. Mutually exclusive with procedure. |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Button caption. Defaults to the procedure name when omitted. |
| `inputFields` | array of `string` | optional | Scalar inputs collected from the user before invoking. |
| `applyTo` | [`workbenchActionApplyTo`](#workbenchactionapplyto) | optional | Folds the procedure's result into the draft as a new row of a collection. |
| `afterAction` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Procedure receiving {draft, result} and returning a patched draft. More general than applyTo; prefer it. |
| `visibleWhen` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Client-tier predicate, e.g. "$root.tipo == 'Expedicao'". |
| `review` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | When true the procedure's result is shown as a field-by-field "proposed changes" dialog; only the ticked fields are folded into the draft (nothing is saved until Save). Not combinable with applyTo, afterAction or checkBalances. |

### `workbenchActionApplyTo`

How an action's result is folded into the draft: appended as a row of a collection.

**Used in:** `workbenchAction.applyTo`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Name of the collection in the draft that this action's result folds into. |
| `mode` | one of `appendRow` | required | Only 'appendRow' is implemented. Prefer the action's `afterAction` procedure for anything else. |
| `map` | map of name to `string` | optional | Target field name -&gt; source path in the procedure result (e.g. "localArmazenagemId": "$resultado.localArmazenagemId"). |

### `workbenchBandPicker`

A modal row picker offered for one band (collection) of the aggregate workbench.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.bandPickers`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `panel` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Source Selection panel the client offers as a modal row picker (C6 "Seleciona Ruas"). |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the picker button. |
| `columns` | array of `string` | optional | Columns shown in the picker. |
| `filter` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | An AND-composed predicate (`field == literal && field == literal`) constraining the candidate rows, enforced server-side; a literal may be `$root.<field>`, the aggregate's root record. The same shape a plain reference field's picker declares. |
| `multiSelect` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | True: several rows may be picked at once. |
| `selectorRef` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a `screens` entry of kind `picker` whose columns, filters, order and `where` are adopted wholesale. This picker's own `filter`, if also given, is combined with the picker screen's using AND. |

### `regionMount`

How an addressable region of the aggregate workbench is filled: generated (default), by an app component, or as a paintable cell grid. A mounted component edits through the workbench store, never around it.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.regions`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render` | one of `generated`, `component`, `cellGrid` | required | "generated" (the platform default; no need to declare it) renders the built-in grid/header. "component" mounts an app-owned JS component (see `component`) in place of the generated rendering for this region. "cellGrid" renders a collection region as the built-in paintable board configured by `cellGrid`. |
| `component` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Required when render is "component": the name registered via window.npdev.regions.register(name, {mount, update, unmount}) in the app's own web/regions/&lt;name&gt;.js (served the same way shell.js auto-injects an app-owned web/theme.css -- never inside npdev-generated/, which is hash-guarded). |
| `cellGrid` | [`cellGrid`](#cellgrid) | optional | With `render: cellGrid`: the board configuration. |

### `cellGrid`

Configuration of a `cellGrid` region: a child collection painted as a board where each row is one cell at (row, column) holding a value chosen from a palette.

**Used in:** `regionMount.cellGrid`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rowField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Integer field of the collection concept holding the cell's 0-based row. |
| `colField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Integer field of the collection concept holding the cell's 0-based column. |
| `valueField` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Field of the collection concept that receives the painted palette row's id; when it is a reference it must target the palette query's concept. |
| `rowsField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional integer field of the aggregate root giving the board's row count. |
| `colsField` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Optional integer field of the aggregate root giving the board's column count. |
| `defaultRows` | `integer` (min 1) | optional | Row count when rowsField is absent or empty (default 10). |
| `defaultCols` | `integer` (min 1) | optional | Column count when colsField is absent or empty (default 10). |
| `layout` | one of `square`, `hexOffset` | optional | "square" (default) or "hexOffset" (odd rows shifted half a cell, cells round -- a honeycomb). |
| `palette` | object | required | Where the paintable values come from.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`query` (`string`; required; min length 1): Query whose rows are the paintable values (each row's id is what gets painted).<br>`labelField` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Palette row field shown as the swatch tooltip.<br>`imageField` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Palette row file field drawn inside the swatch and the cell.<br>`colorField` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Palette row #hex field used as the swatch/cell colour (and behind the image). |

### `transactionHooks`

Closed set of hooks around the aggregate workbench: when the draft loads, when a field changes, before an action and on validate and commit. Each names a procedure or flow.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.hooks`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onLoad` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Invoked once after the workbench draft is first loaded, before the first render; the returned state becomes the initial draft. |
| `onFieldChange` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Retires transaction.metadata.recompute. Invoked (debounced) on every cell edit; the returned state patches the draft. |
| `beforeAction` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | A guard invoked before any declared workbench action's procedure runs; a non-ok result aborts the action with no invoke. |
| `onValidate` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a procedure or flow run before the commit; a failure vetoes it. |
| `onCommit` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Name of a procedure or flow run after the commit. |

### `transactionDerivedField`

A display-only value recomputed from the current workbench draft, either in the browser (`expression`) or on the server (`procedure`).

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.derivedFields`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the derived value. |
| `tier` | one of `client`, `server` (default `"client"`) | optional | Client (default): `expression` is evaluated locally by the browser (the same narrow expression language the retired `derived` key used). server: `procedure` is invoked over the draft. |
| `expression` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For the `client` tier: the expression evaluated in the browser over the draft. |
| `procedure` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For the `server` tier: the procedure invoked over the draft. |

### `transactionUiState`

A piece of transient UI state (for example a record-type toggle) that `$ui.<name>` predicates on the surface can read. Never part of the commit payload.

**Used in:** `autoPanelSurface.uiState`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | Caption of the control that changes the state. |
| `values` | array of `string` (min items 1) | required | The closed set of values this control offers; a $ui.&lt;name&gt; predicate may only compare against one of these. |
| `default` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | Seeded on load. Defaults to values[0] when absent. |

## 10. Pack

A versioned, reusable bundle of concepts, flows, roles and screens that a model imports with the `packs` root key. This section lists the two shapes used to reference other files and packs; the keys of a pack file itself are in section 0.

### `packRef`

One entry of the root `packs` array: a pack the model consumes, either from a local file (`$ref`) or from a remote coordinate (`from`, resolved only from the local pack cache pinned by `npdev.lock`). Exactly one of the two.

**Used in:** `packs` (model root)

**Conditional rules:**

- Exactly one of `$ref`, `from` must be present.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$ref` | `string` (min length 1; pattern `^(?![A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:)(?!/).*\.json$`) | optional | Relative path of a local pack file (`.json`). Mutually exclusive with `from`. |
| `from` | `string` (min length 1; must match the schema's pattern) | optional | Remote pack coordinate -- oci://registry/repository:tag (or @sha256:&lt;digest&gt;), or git+&lt;transport&gt;://url[//subpath]@tag. Mutually exclusive with $ref, which stays local-file-only by design -- npdev generate resolves a 'from' pack ONLY from the local content-addressed cache via npdev.lock, never over the network; see NetworkPolicy. |
| `as` | `string` (min length 1; pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`) | optional | Optional alias overriding the pack's own identifier as the namespace prefix in this model. |
| `allowSideBySide` | `boolean` | optional | Tolerate this direct import's real pack id colliding, at a different major version, with a pack id resolved transitively elsewhere in this model's dependency graph -- normally a hard refusal. Requires `as`, since the direct import must stay distinguishable from the transitive one. |

Example:

```json
{
  "$ref": "packs/identity/pack.json",
  "as": "identity"
}
```

### `localModelRef`

A pointer to a local JSON file that holds one item (for example one concept). It may be written wherever a model array accepts an object kind. The path is relative, ends in `.json` and may not climb out of the model's folder.

**Used in:** `backOffice.pages`, `concepts` (model root and pack file), `domainTypes` (model root and pack file), `capabilities` (model root and pack file), `events` (model root and pack file), `flows` (model root and pack file), `queries` (model root and pack file), `conversions` (model root and pack file), `panels` (model root and pack file), `autoPanels` (model root and pack file), `roles` (pack file), `sequences` (pack file), `functions` (pack file), `experiences` (pack file), `screens` (pack file), `seeds` (pack file), `propertyScopes` (pack file), `properties` (pack file), `fragments` (pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$ref` | `string` (min length 1; must match the schema's pattern) | required | Relative path of the JSON file that holds the item. |

## 11. Module

Composition and evolution of a model: bounded contexts (`modules`, each a fragment file) and declarative data conversions that run at boot when the schema changes.

### `context`

A bounded context (module): a named fragment file whose concepts, queries, panels and flows belong to the context. Other contexts reference its members as `context::Concept` and must list it in the fragment's `imports`.

**Used in:** `modules` (model root)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1; pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`) | required | The context's name; the prefix of its members (`name::Concept`). |
| `$ref` | `string` (min length 1; must match the schema's pattern) | required | Relative path of the fragment file whose members belong to the context. |
| `physicallyIsolate` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | True: the context's data is stored apart from the rest of the app. |

### `conversion`

A declarative data conversion that runs at boot when the schema changes (rename, split, merge, lookup, convert, coalesce, case), compiled to the same hook shape the conversion runner already executes. Exactly one of `op` or `javaHook`.

**Used in:** `conversions` (model root and pack file)

**Conditional rules:**

- Requires exactly one of `op`, `javaHook`.
- When `javaHook` is present: requires `claims`.
- When `op` is `copy` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `to`.
- When `op` is `split` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `into`.
- When `op` is `lookup` and `op` is present: requires `match`, `set`.
- When `op` is `merge` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `to`; `from` must be of type array.
- When `op` is `convert` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `to`; `from` must be of type string.
- When `op` is `coalesce` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `to`; `from` must be of type array.
- When `op` is `case` and `op` is present: requires `from`, `to`, `when`; `from` must be of type string.

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Unique id of the conversion; it names the generated hook directory `db/conversion-hooks/<id>`. |
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The concept whose rows are converted. |
| `op` | one of `copy`, `split`, `lookup`, `merge`, `convert`, `coalesce`, `case` | optional | The conversion: `copy` a field, `split` one into several, `lookup` a value from another concept, `merge` several into one, `convert` the type, `coalesce` the first non-empty of several or `case` map literal values. |
| `javaHook` | object | optional | Runs id's conversion as a Java method in the isolated plugin pool instead of generated SQL. source is a source-root path (same shape plugin:java-source's implementation.sourceRoot uses), class the FQCN, method the method name -- admitted through the same bytecode/AST escape-detection a plugin:java-source mount goes through.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`source` (`string`; required; min length 1): Source-root path of the Java class, in the same shape a mounted code extension uses.<br>`class` (`string`; required; min length 1): Fully qualified name of the class.<br>`method` (`string`; required; min length 1): Name of the method that performs the conversion. |
| `claims` | array of `string` (min items 1) | optional | Required with javaHook -- the plain field names on concept this hook resolves (every other op derives its claims automatically from to; a Java hook cannot be statically analyzed that way). Each name is compiler-checked against concept's real fields, same X0 discipline as to. |
| `from` | `string` or array of `string` | optional | A plain field name for copy/split/convert/case; an array of 2+ field names for merge/coalesce. |
| `to` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | The target field the result is written to. |
| `into` | array of [`conversionSplitTarget`](#conversionsplittarget) (min items 1) | optional | For `split`: the target fields and which part each receives. |
| `match` | [`conversionLookupMatch`](#conversionlookupmatch) | optional | For `lookup`: how the source row is found. |
| `set` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | For `lookup`: the field of this concept that receives the id of the matched row. |
| `with` | `string` | optional | merge's separator, concatenated between each pair of 'from' fields. Optional; defaults to "" (no separator) when omitted. |
| `when` | array of [`conversionCaseWhen`](#conversioncasewhen) (min items 1) | optional | case's 1+ literal equals/then branches, evaluated in declared order, first match wins. |
| `else` | `string` | optional | case's default literal when no 'when' clause matches. Optional; a row matching nothing and declaring no 'else' is left NULL. |

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "split-name",
  "concept": "Person",
  "op": "split",
  "from": "fullName",
  "into": [
    {
      "field": "firstName",
      "take": "before-first-space"
    },
    {
      "field": "lastName",
      "take": "after-first-space"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `conversionSplitTarget`

One target of a `split` conversion.

**Used in:** `conversion.into`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The target field that receives a part. |
| `take` | one of `before-first-space`, `after-first-space` | required | Which part: `before-first-space` or `after-first-space`. |

### `conversionLookupMatch`

How a `lookup` conversion finds the row to copy a value from.

**Used in:** `conversion.match`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `concept` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The concept whose rows are matched. |
| `on` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Field of that concept compared with this concept's `equals` field. |
| `equals` | `string` (min length 1) | required | Field of the converted concept (the one the conversion belongs to) whose value must equal the matched concept's `on` field. |

### `conversionCaseWhen`

One branch of a `case` conversion.

**Used in:** `conversion.when`

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `equals` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The literal value to compare with. |
| `then` | `string` | required | The literal value written when it matches. |

## 12. Property

Runtime configuration resolved through a scoped cascade (for example tenant, then user), plus the app-level setting for delegating work to an outside AI.

### `property`

A typed runtime setting resolved through the scoped cascade of `propertyScopes`: the most specific scope with a value wins, otherwise the `default`. Read in expressions as `$prop.<name>`.

**Used in:** `properties` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The property's name, read in expressions as `$prop.<name>`. |
| `type` | one of `string`, `int`, `boolean`, `enum`, `date` | required | A closed set -- no objects, no arrays. The property cascade resolves one typed value per key, never a blob. |
| `default` | any value | required | The least-specific level of the cascade -- there is no 'system' scope; a property with no row set at any declared scope resolves to this value. Must match 'type' (checked by PropertyValidation, not by this schema alone, since JSON Schema cannot express 'shape of one field depends on another field's value' compactly here). |
| `settableAt` | array of `string` | optional | Which declared propertyScopes[].name values may hold a row for this property. Every name here must be declared in propertyScopes -- checked at compile time, not by this schema. |
| `label` | [`localizableLabel`](#localizablelabel) | optional | The name shown in the admin surface. |
| `securityRelevant` | `boolean` (default `false`) | optional | A real flag with teeth: a securityRelevant property is FORBIDDEN inside $prop.* references in access.read/access.write (A4's hard rule) and is visually marked + requires an elevated role in the generated admin surface (A5). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "maxDiscount",
  "type": "int",
  "default": 10,
  "settableAt": [
    "tenant"
  ]
}
```

### `propertyScope`

One level of the property cascade. The order of `propertyScopes` is the resolution order, most specific first.

**Used in:** `propertyScopes` (model root and pack file)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` (min length 1) | required | The scope's name, referenced by `settableAt`. |
| `from` | `string` (min length 1) | optional | How this scope's id resolves from ExecutionContext at authentication time -- '$ctx.tenantId', '$user.id', or '$user.&lt;tagName&gt;'. Absent/blank for the implicit root scope (always $ctx.tenantId -- every request already carries a tenant, so the least-specific declared scope needs no expression). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "user",
  "from": "$user.id"
}
```

### `externalAi`

The app's opt-in to delegating work to an outside AI. Absent means denied: no code path may send anything to a vendor without this block. It selects the vendors, defines named prompts that flows run and sets cost limits.

**Used in:** `externalAi` (model root)

| Keyword | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `egress` | one of `denied`, `packOnly`, `apiEnabled` (default `"denied"`) | optional | Denied: no egress possible. packOnly: packs may be built and reviewed locally (e.g. air-gapped paste-transport) but never auto-sent. apiEnabled: the external-ai-http adapter may call a configured vendor. |
| `vendors` | array of `string` | optional | Vendor ids this app has opted into -- each must be an appVendor provider id of the NPDev AI catalogue (NPDevCli/ai-providers.json; `npdev ai providers` lists them) or the id of one of this model's own externalAi.providers, or SemanticValidator rejects it. Required non-empty when egress is not "denied" -- SemanticValidator rejects egress-enabled with no vendor configured. |
| `providers` | array of object | optional | This app's own AI endpoints, beyond the providers the NPDev AI catalogue ships -- e.g. a company gateway or a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server. Each one is an app vendor of this app only, and must still be listed in vendors to be called. The id must not be a shipped catalogue id. Its key is always read from NPDEV_EXTERNALAI_&lt;ID&gt;_API_KEY (the id upper-cased, '-' as '_'), so a model can never point an endpoint at another provider's key.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`id` (`string`; required; pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`): The vendor id vendors[] and prompts[].vendor use.<br>`name` (`string`; optional; min length 1): A display name; defaults to the id.<br>`protocol` (one of `openai-chat`, `anthropic-messages`, `gemini-native`; required): The wire format the endpoint speaks.<br>`baseUrl` (`string`; required; min length 1): The endpoint root, e.g. https://ai.example.com/v1 (openai-chat appends /chat/completions, anthropic-messages /messages). https, or http only to a loopback host; no query or fragment.<br>`needsKey` (`boolean`; optional; default `true`): False for a keyless endpoint (a local server). true: the app reads NPDEV_EXTERNALAI_&lt;ID&gt;_API_KEY.<br>`defaultModel` (`string`; required; min length 1): The model a prompt naming none calls.<br>`price` (object; optional): USD per million tokens, for every model of this provider; feeds externalAi.limits.monthlyCostCapUsd. Absent: unpriced (0) unless npdev.externalai.price.&lt;id&gt;.* is set. |
| `prompts` | array of object | optional | Named prompts a flow runs with capabilityCall externalAi.generate, args ["&lt;prompt name&gt;", "$input"]. The vendor's answer is validated against outputSchema before the flow sees it.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`name` (`string`; required; min length 1): The prompt's name, the first argument of `externalAi.generate`.<br>`description` (`string`; optional): A sentence saying what the prompt is for.<br>`vendor` (`string`; optional; min length 1): One of externalAi.vendors. Give vendor (and optionally model), or profile -- not both; the validator names the problem when neither or both are set.<br>`profile` (`string`; optional; min length 1): A profile of the NPDev AI catalogue (e.g. 'fast', 'claude'; `npdev ai profiles`) instead of vendor + model. The generator resolves it to the profile's provider, model and effort; that provider must be in externalAi.vendors.<br>`effort` (one of `low`, `medium`, `high`; optional): How hard the model should think. Overrides a profile's effort. Sent only to a vendor that has such a setting (Anthropic: output_config.effort); dropped for the others.<br>`model` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Overrides the vendor profile's default model.<br>`template` (`string`; required; min length 1): Prompt text with {{field}} placeholders filled from the call's input map (dotted paths allowed; lists/maps are inserted as JSON).<br>`image` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Input field holding a file reference (an image) sent alongside the text for vision.<br>`outputSchema` (object; required): JSON Schema the answer must satisfy; the vendor is asked for JSON of this shape and anything else fails the step.<br>`maxOutputTokens` (`integer`; optional; min 1): Upper bound on the length of the vendor's answer.<br>`review` (one of `required`, `optional`, `none`; optional): Whether a human reviews this prompt's answer before anything applies it. 'none' (default) keeps today's behaviour. 'required' makes the validator demand that every flow calling the prompt parks the answer on an awaitEvent step whose task.proposal.value is the call's output, directly after the call (and bars procedures from calling it). 'optional' is recorded and audited but not enforced. |
| `limits` | object | optional | Each value names a declared properties[] key, resolved through the scoped-property cascade per call. Absent = unbounded on that axis.<br>Keys written inside it:<br>`callsPerUserPerDay` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Property (type int) bounding generate calls per user per UTC day.<br>`monthlyCostCapUsd` (`string`; optional; min length 1): Property (type int = whole USD, or string = decimal USD like "2.50") bounding the tenant's estimated AI spend per UTC calendar month. |

## Coverage

- Keywords documented: 759 (719 model + 40 pack), the same set the keyword budget freezes.
- Meaning taken from the schema's own `description`: 255.
- Meaning written in `scripts/policy/dsl-keyword-meanings/`: 504.
- `scripts/quality/check-dsl-keyword-reference.py` fails when a keyword has no meaning, when the meanings data names a keyword the schema no longer has, or when this page is stale against the schema.
